Subject: POC trial plan & model selection — next steps

Hi Alex / Priya,

Great to speak earlier — thanks for walking through RetailCo's search & support use cases. Quick recap from our side plus proposed next steps for the POC/trial so we can align on scope and success criteria: 

Summary of needs:
- Primary: Improving search relevance and support deflection for English + Spanish product pages.
- Volume: ~1.5M monthly queries, peak 800 qps for search; support volume smaller (~20k/mo).
- Constraints: Latency target < 300ms p95 for search suggestions; data residency in US.

Proposed POC scope (2-week technical trial + 4-week evaluation):
1) Week 0-2 (trial): Ship a hosted trial endpoint + sample ingestion of 50k product pages. Run automated evals and live A/B on ~10k queries.
2) Week 3-6 (evaluation): Broader traffic split, measure relevance metrics and business KPIs (click-through, support deflection).

Success criteria (to sign off POC):
- Search relevance: +8–12% improvement in mean reciprocal rank (MRR) vs baseline on heldout query set.
- Support deflection: >15% reduction in tickets for targeted flows.
- Latency: p95 < 300ms for suggestion & first-token generation.
- Cost: expected per-query token cost below $0.004 (for production sizing).

Model selection recommendation for the trial (initial + fallback):
- Primary: Mistral-Instruct-7B (quantized) — good balance of latency, multilingual abilities, and instruction following for reranking & generation.
- Fallback: Llama-2-13B (int8) — slightly heavier but more robust on longer-context relevance; route to fallback on latency/throughput constraints.
- For heavy multilingual extraction (Spanish + Portuguese), we recommend augmenting with a FLAN-T5-XXL reranker for specific extraction tasks if we see precision shortfalls.

Ownership & next steps:
- Ben (me): coordinate contractual trial terms, HubSpot deal RC-5542, kick off infra access.
- Marissa: own the technical onboarding, ingestion, and evaluation harness (model matrix + metrics).
- RetailCo (Alex / Priya): provide sample dataset (50k pages) and baseline query logs + 2 evaluation query sets (search & support).

Attachments: redwood-poc-scope-v1.pdf and model-comparison-matrix.xlsx attached.

Can you confirm the success criteria above and whether the 6-week timeline looks ok? If yes we'll send a brief statement of work and schedule an onboarding call for Monday.

Thanks,
Ben

Hi Alex / Priya —

Quick technical notes to answer your model question and lay out the eval plan Marissa-style: 

Why Mistral-Instruct-7B primary:
- Strong instruction-following for reranking and short-response generation with lower compute footprint (good for suggestion latency).
- We have quantized pipelines (int4/int8) available in the Redwood runtime that keep p95 latency under 250ms on our default config for average search sizes.

When we'll route to Llama-2-13B fallback:
- If we observe >4% absolute drop in MRR for Spanish queries versus baseline in the first 1k eval queries, we'll automatically spin Llama-2-13B for Spanish-heavy batches while keeping Mistral for English. This is driven by a simple policy in our smart routing layer.

Evaluation harness (what we'll run during trial):
- Offline: relevance eval (MRR, NDCG) on heldout sets (English / Spanish), precision/recall for entity extraction tasks.
- Online: 10k-query A/B (50/50) measuring CTR, time-to-first-byte, and ticket open rate for support flows.
- Quality gates: fail POC if MRR improvement <5% on English AND Spanish precision <90% (we can relax Spanish precision if sample size small).

Data/security notes:
- We'll request a temporary role-based S3 ingest or secure SFTP. Redwood will not persist raw query logs beyond the trial window unless you opt-in; we'll produce a deletion certificate after trial.

Next steps I will own:
- Share the model-comparison-matrix.xlsx with expected latency/cost tradeoffs by model and quant config (attached).
- Kick off ingestion once Ben confirms SOW & RetailCo provides dataset.

I'll set up a technical kickoff for Monday 9am PT — Ben, can you confirm?
